patent_pending: U.S. Provisional Patent Application No. 64/198,910, filed November 14, 2026 — patent pending. The governed-crossing and receipt-pair mechanism served by this endpoint is subject matter of the pending application.

provider.role: service provider — governance and receipting over machine-economy transactions already flowing on existing rails

offered_resources.description: Admissibility evaluation of a machine-proposed transaction or action at the signing boundary, under the ecosystem disposition grammar (ALLOW / DENY / FAIL_CLOSED). Only ALLOW commits, at the signing boundary this service controls; execution paths that do not pass through this endpoint's evaluation are outside that boundary.

Issuance of a dual-recorded receipt pair for a governed crossing: receipts attach to transitions, not transactions, and one boundary crossing yields one matched pair — two records, one per side of the crossing, hash-chained — constituting a portable settlement proof: the pair is verifiable by either side against the chain's anchors without trusting the other party's internal log. Independent retention of the pair by the customer is not yet demonstrated; it is the subject of BUILD-Q-44. A refused or fail-closed attempt likewise produces a receipt: the refusal record.

Agreement receipting under the admitted scope ME-AGREE-01 (BUILD-Q-49, admitted 2026-11-18): a bot or agent that has reached an agreement — deal terms accepted by both sides — records it as a governed crossing with action "record-agreement" before treating the deal as final. The crossing carries the commit-time evidence object (authority, delegation, evidence_refs, exclusions, policy ME-POLICY-01, validity_at_commit) and the resource names the agreement being receipted (form: agreement-record:<agreement reference>). On ALLOW the crossing issues the matched receipt pair for the agreement; on NON-ALLOW the attempt is refused or fails closed with the six-field disposition and a refusal receipt, and the fee position follows the offer's active pricing mode. Priced at the full-evaluation tier: the governance fee (15,000 micro-USDC) plus the settlement charge quoted at challenge time (BUILD-Q-43 / offer v07); the challenge amount is the total authorized.

modes.description: The fee is charged per evaluation regardless of outcome: an ALLOW, a DENY, and a FAIL_CLOSED each bear the fee for the unit of compute they consumed. This is the ACTIVE mode under the current operating configuration.

The ALLOW disposition price covers all dispositions: the cost of refused evaluations is amortized into the ALLOW price; a refusal draws no separate charge, and its compute is paid for through the ALLOW price. This mode is NOT active.
